1.explanation: The logic for ignoreRestSiblings lives in lib/rules/no-unused-vars.js – it checks for RestElement siblings only in VariableDeclarator patterns, not in function parameters. To fix this, that rule file must be updated to treat ObjectPattern parameters with a RestElement the same way (ignoring the sibling properties). Additionally, tests in tests/lib/rules/no-unused-vars.js should be extended to cover the function-parameter destructuring scenario so that future regressions are caught.

2.explanation:
• lib/rules/no-unused-vars.js contains the core logic for reporting unused variables. It currently only omits unused siblings of a RestElement in VariableDeclarator patterns and does not apply the same filter when the pattern appears in function parameters. 

• tests/lib/rules/no-unused-vars.js is the unit-test suite for this rule. It has coverage for ignoreRestSiblings in variable declarations but lacks any tests for function parameter rest patterns, so this case slips through. 

• docs/rules/no-unused-vars.md documents the ignoreRestSiblings option and examples only in the context of variable declarations. It needs updating to clarify and illustrate support for function parameters once the implementation is fixed.
2.bug_scenario: When using object rest/destructuring in function parameters with the ESLint “no-unused-vars” rule and the “ignoreRestSiblings” option enabled, sibling properties of a RestElement (for example, the “children” parameter in `({ children, ...props }) => {}`) are still reported as unused even though they should be ignored. In other words, `ignoreRestSiblings: true` works for variable declarations but not for function argument patterns.
